Market implies ~85% for Andreeva (-850) and the fundamentals agree: world #5, career-high ranking, 40-13 in 2026, and a straight-sets win over Tjen (6-1, 7-6) just two weeks ago in Cincinnati. Tjen is a quality top-40 player having a breakthrough year, so she can keep a set competitive, but Andreeva's return game, movement, and big-match experience make an upset unlikely.

Market implies ~60% for Ostapenko (-170). The 30 seed has far better hard-court pedigree (Grand Slam champion, #32) while Maria is 5-12 on hard in 2026 with her wins coming almost entirely on grass (16-5). Counters: Ostapenko is erratic, lost early in Toronto and Cincinnati, and retired against Maria at Eastbourne. Maria's slice is awkward, but on a consistent Laykold bounce Ostapenko's first-strike power should prevail if her body holds up.

No reliable market line available. On paper the #24 seed (#25 rank) should be a heavy favorite over #109: bigger serve, more power, and far greater Slam experience. However, Potapova carries real fitness doubt after a back-related withdrawal in Monterrey and straight-set losses in Toronto and Cincinnati, while Semenistaja arrives match-sharp from qualifying. Ranking gap suggests ~70%+, but the injury risk and Semenistaja's recent form pull this down toward the low 60s.

Market implies ~82% for Mertens (-600), matching model estimates (~81.5%). Mertens (#20, seed 23) brings elite consistency, return quality, and hard-court experience against a #107-ranked opponent, and she arrives in form off a Monterrey final. The only caveat is the quick turnaround from a physically demanding week in Mexico, which slightly tempers the edge but does not threaten the outcome in a best-of-3 against this opposition.

Market implies ~74% for Jovic (-350); models cluster around 72%. The 18-year-old American (#14, seed 14) has had a breakout 2026 with an Australian Open QF, Wimbledon R16, and quality hard-court wins in Toronto and Cincinnati, plus home support. Frech (#41) is a solid counterpuncher who beat Ostapenko in Cincinnati and made the US Open third round last year, so she can extend rallies and keep sets tight, but Jovic's superior firepower and serve make her a clear favorite.

Market prices Jeanjean as a clear favorite (-208, ~64% no-vig) and she holds the stronger trailing-12-month and current-season form. Rus is a crafty lefty veteran but is well past her peak, is clay-leaning, and her hard-court results have thinned; Jeanjean's age profile and recent level justify the edge, though neither is a natural hard-courter so the match could stay competitive in humid conditions.

Bartunkova (#34) is a rising hard-court talent and the market makes her a heavy favorite (-450, ~78% no-vig). Sherif (#52) is a clay specialist whose 2026 titles came on clay; she has played only four outdoor hard matches this season, losing three. Surface mismatch and ranking gap strongly favor the Czech.

Near pick'em market (Linette -120 / Jones -103) with a slight lean to Linette. The Pole is the higher-ranked, more experienced hard-courter (13-12 on hard in 2026) and owns the better trailing-12-month level, while Jones has been the better current-year performer and came through qualifying. Experience and Slam-level hard-court pedigree tip a genuinely tight contest marginally to Linette.

Effectively a coin flip in the market (Oliynykova -110 / Brantmeier -112). Oliynykova is the established tour player at #46 and has dominated when priced as favorite recently, while Brantmeier is a talented but lightly ranked American wildcard with comparable second-serve numbers and home support. Ranking, tour mileage, and big-match experience give the Ukrainian the slimmest of edges.

Gauff, the #4 seed and home favorite, is priced at -2500 (~91% no-vig) and arrives with strong summer hard-court form including a Cincinnati title run. Sonmez (#53) is a steady counterpuncher but lacks the weapons to trouble Gauff's defense, return game, and athleticism over two sets. One of the most lopsided matchups of the round.

Eala (#18 seed) is in excellent 2026 hard-court form, leads the head-to-head 1-0, and is priced at -422 (~77% no-vig). Her left-handed patterns, movement, and baseline consistency match up well against Stoiana (#122), whose game is better suited to clay. Home crowd may keep Stoiana competitive in patches, but Eala's ranking, experience, and form make her a strong favorite.
Sakkari is the seeded veteran with solid hard-court results, and the moneyline (-150) makes her a modest favorite. Montgomery has momentum and home support, keeping this competitive.
Starodubtseva is ranked much higher (#58 vs #123) and owns the recent hard-court form edge. The market (-275) and 1-0 head-to-head record support her strongly.
Rybakina is the No. 2 seed and a top hard-court contender. Frodin is a low-ranked qualifier with little main-tour pedigree, and the market (-2800) prices a near-certain outcome.
Bencic is the No. 12 seed with better 2026 hard-court numbers and a decisive serve/return edge. Putintseva's recent slump and the market (-508) leave her a clear underdog.
Lys is favored by the market (-178) and holds a 1-0 hard-court head-to-head lead. Knutson’s qualifying momentum and Lys’s winless back-to-back match streak in 2026 narrow the gap.
Keys has the seeding, far more Grand Slam experience, and strong summer form. Korneeva is a dangerous young qualifier, but the market (-284) and Keys’s firepower give the American the edge.

Bondar is favored by the market (-184) and ranking (#73), and leads the head-to-head. Havlickova arrives with confidence from qualifying, including a win over Moyuka Uchijima, but Bondar’s tour-level consistency is the safer pick.

Market prices Badosa as a moderate favorite (-135) despite her lower ranking, reflecting her former top-tier pedigree and strong July clay/125 form. Kasatkina is competitive on hard courts but the market and recent fitness rest favor Badosa.

predictions.matchup: Darja Vidmanova vs Jessica Bouzas Maneiro
predictions.reasoning: The moneyline is essentially a coin flip (-106 / -116), with Bouzas Maneiro priced as the slightest favorite. Vidmanova has the ranking edge and aggressive baseline game, but the market sees the match as dead even.

Andreeva is the 5th seed and heavy market favorite (-850), and she already beat Tjen on hard courts in Cincinnati this month. Tjen is a capable opponent but the gap in ranking, form and pricing is large.

Ostapenko is the seeded player with the superior hard-court pedigree and the market prices her around -170. Maria is dangerous and has fitness edge, but at 39 and with limited hard-court upside she is the underdog.
Potapova is the #24 seed facing a player outside the top 100. Recent back/fitness issues keep confidence from High, but the ranking, seeding and hard-court experience gap should carry her through.
Mertens is the seeded top-20 veteran and a clear market favorite (-600). Quevedo is ranked outside the top 100 and lacks the consistency to upset a steady hard-court performer like Mertens.
Jovic is the #14 seed with breakout 2026 Slam results and strong recent hard-court form. Frech is in decent touch but the market (-350) and home-court upside clearly favor the American.

The market prices Jeanjean around -200, implying roughly a 64% win chance. Rus offers value at plus-money, but Jeanjean's recent form and the oddsmakers' confidence make her the rightful favorite on hard courts in New York.

Bartunkova is a clear -450 favorite and has the superior hard-court record this season. Sherif has struggled on outdoor hard courts, winning only one of four matches, and Bartunkova's higher ranking and form support a strong win probability.

The moneyline is essentially a coin flip, with Linette slightly favored at -120. Linette's greater experience and slightly better trailing-12-month record give her a narrow edge, but Jones's current-year form keeps this very close.

The market has this as a virtual pick'em, with Brantmeier a microscopic -112 favorite. Home-court support as a wildcard and marginally steadier second-serve numbers nudge the prediction her way, but the match could easily go either way.

Gauff is a dominant -2500 favorite, implying over 90% win probability. The world No. 4 and No. 4 seed brings elite hard-court defense, serve, and recent form, making a Sonmez upset extremely unlikely.

Eala is priced around -400 as the 17th seed and world No. 18, and she owns a 1-0 head-to-head edge over Stoiana. Eala's left-handed baseline consistency and strong 2026 hard-court form make her a clear favorite.
